pairs.why: A's table and stools fill the card at close scale with little empty ground, like the real table, while B shrinks the hero and leaves a lot of open lawn and path.
A keeps the truss as a horizontal bar cropped at the top edge, with a large fixture centered below it, as in the real card; B tilts the truss diagonally.
A's clock is centered and fills the card with small margins, like the real one; B sits on a floor strip with a ground shadow that the real card doesn't have.
A's dome is larger and more central, so it reads faster at thumbnail size, as the real hero objects do; B's smaller dome shares the card with a big crater and a side pod.
A has a horizontal truss cropped at the top edge and a big fixture, matching the real framing; B's diagonal truss and smaller fixture leave more empty space.
Both chairs have almost the same scale, placement and margins, so composition gives no reason to choose.
A's hat is large and tilted at a three-quarter angle, and fills the card like the real hero items; B is a smaller, flatter, centered hat with more empty space.
B's rocket is bigger and fills the card edge to edge on a diagonal, like the real submarine; A's rocket is smaller and leaves more empty margin.
